questions.stem:
The company Seafield requires contractors to record the number of hours they work each week. A random sample of 38 weeks is taken and the number of hours worked per week by contractor Kiana is summarised in the stem and leaf diagram below.

$\begin{array}{c|ccccccccccc|c}\text{Stem} & \text{Leaf} & & & & & & & & & & & \\ \hline 1 & 4 & 4 & 4 & 5 & 5 & 5 & 6 & 6 & 9 & 9 & 9 & (11)\\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 2 & 3 & 3 & 4 & 4 & 4 & w & 9 & & (10)\\ 3 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 & 7 & 7 & 9 & & (10)\\ 4 & 1 & 1 & 2 & 3 & & & & & & & & (4)\\ 5 & 1 & 9 & & & & & & & & & & (2)\\ 6 & 4 & & & & & & & & & & & (1)\end{array}$   Key: $3|2$ means 32

The quartiles for this distribution are summarised in the table below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline Q_1 & Q_2 & Q_3\\ \hline x & 26 & y\\ \hline\end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $w=8$ B1
$x=19$ B1
$y=37$ B1
Cao. May be seen in table before part (a). $w=28$ is first B0.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Kiana is looking for outliers in the data. She decides to classify as outliers any observations greater than
$Q_3 + 1.0 \times (Q_3-Q_1)$
(b) Showing your working clearly, identify any outliers that Kiana finds.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $"37"+1\times("37"-"19")$ [=55] M1
59 and 64 A1ft
Calculation for the outliers using their lower quartile and upper quartile. Allow "their upper quartile" + "their IQR" for this mark i.e. 37+18. For identifying 59 and 64 as outliers from correct working. Ft the identification of outlier(s) (if any) from "their 55" from their shown calculation. Answer only is M0A0.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Draw a box plot for these data in the space provided on the grid opposite.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) For a box with at least one whisker drawn M1
14 for lowest whisker, 26 for median, "19" and "37" plotted for quartiles ft their values for quartiles A1ft
Upper whisker at 51 or "their 51" plus "their outliers" plotted but there must be at least one outlier for this mark. Condone upper whisker at "their 55". NB award A0 if there is more than one whisker at either end A1ft

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Use the formula
$\text{skewness} = \dfrac{(Q_3-Q_2)-(Q_2-Q_1)}{(Q_3-Q_1)}$
to find the skewness of these data. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
(2)

parts.label: e
parts.text:
Kiana's new employer, Landacre, wishes to know the average number of hours per week she worked during her employment at Seafield to help calculate the cost of employing her.
(e) Explain why Landacre might prefer to know Kiana's mean, rather than median, number of hours worked per week.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) E.g. 'The mean uses all the data' B1
A correct reason which supports Landacre's use of the mean or rejects their use of the median. Allow comment relating to (slight) positive skew so mean > median so Landacre will know the larger average they will have to pay. Comments about skewness/symmetry on their own score B0. Mean includes the outliers is B1. Condone Median is not affected by the outliers for B1. Mean is more accurate is B0.

questions.stem:
Gill buys a bag of logs to use in her stove. The lengths, $l\,\text{cm}$, of the 88 logs in the bag are summarised in the table below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Length }(l) & \text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 15<l\leqslant 20 & 19\\ \hline 20<l\leqslant 25 & 35\\ \hline 25<l\leqslant 27 & 16\\ \hline 27<l\leqslant 30 & 15\\ \hline 30<l\leqslant 40 & 3\\ \hline\end{array}$

A histogram is drawn to represent these data.
The bar representing logs with length $27<l\leqslant 30$ has a width of $1.5\,\text{cm}$ and a height of $4\,\text{cm}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Calculate the width and height of the bar representing log lengths of $20<l\leqslant 25$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Width = 2.5 (cm) B1
Height $=\left(\dfrac{35}{15}\times 6\right)\div "2.5"$ or $\frac{4}{5}\times 7$ or 6cm$^2$=15 (logs) or 14cm$^2$=35 (logs) oe M1
=5.6 (cm) A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Correct method to relate area to number of logs (may be implied by "their w" $\times$ "their h" = 14)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use linear interpolation to estimate the median of $l$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) Median $=[20]+\dfrac{25}{35}\times 5$ allow $[20]+\dfrac{25.5}{35}\times 5$ M1
=23.57… allow 23.64… awrt 23.6 A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 For a correct fraction multiplied by 5. Allow working downwards e.g. $[25]-\frac{10}{35}\times 5$
- A1 Correct answer from correct working. Allow exact fraction.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The maximum length of log Gill can use in her stove is 26 cm.
Gill estimates, using linear interpolation, that $x$ logs from the bag will fit into her stove.
(c) Show that $x = 62$
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $19+35+8 (=62^*)$ or $88-3-15-8 (=62^*)$ B1cso*
A correct calculation seen. Allow $\frac{1}{2}(16)$ for 8. Allow equivalent methods $\frac{x-54}{70-54}=\frac{26-25}{27-25}$ or $\frac{54+70}{2}$. Minimum working required $54+8$ or $70-8$ or $\frac{54+70}{2}$. NB: $26+x=88 \to x=62$ is B0.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Gill randomly selects 4 logs from the bag.
(d) Using $x = 62$, find the probability that all 4 logs will fit into her stove.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) P(4 logs fit) $=\left(\dfrac{62}{88}\right)\times\left(\dfrac{61}{87}\right)\times\left(\dfrac{60}{86}\right)\times\left(\dfrac{59}{85}\right)$ M1
=0.23922…. awrt 0.239 A1
SC: With replacement awrt 0.246 scores M1A0
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 For $\left(\frac{n}{88}\right)\times\left(\frac{n-1}{87}\right)\times\left(\frac{n-2}{86}\right)\times\left(\frac{n-3}{85}\right)$ (allow any n < 88)

parts.label: e(i)
parts.text:
The weights, $W$ grams, of the logs in the bag are coded using $y=0.5w-255$ and summarised by
$n=88 \quad \sum y = 924 \quad \sum y^2 = 12862$
(e) Calculate
(i) the mean of $W$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e)(i) mean of $y=\dfrac{924}{88}[=10.5]$ M1
mean of $w=("10.5"+255)\times 2$ M1
=531 A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Correct method for finding mean of y (implied by 10.5) or for equation $0.5\sum w-88\times 255=924$
- M1 Correct method for finding mean of w or $\sum w=46728$ and $\frac{46728}{88}$
- A1 Cao

parts.label: e(ii)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e)(ii) variance of $y=\dfrac{12862}{88}-("10.5")^2[=35.909...]$ M1
variance of $w="35.909"\times 4$ or $"35.909"\div 0.5^2$ M1
=143.636… awrt 144 A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Correct method for finding variance of y (implied by awrt 35.9) or $0.25\sum w^2+255^2\times 88-255\sum w=12862$
- M1 Correct method for finding variance of w or $\sum w^2=24825208$ and $\frac{24825208}{88}-"531"^2$

questions.stem:
The events $H$ and $W$ are such that
$\mathrm{P}(H)=\dfrac{3}{8} \qquad \mathrm{P}(H\cup W)=\dfrac{3}{4}$
Given that $H$ and $W$ are independent,

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\mathrm{P}(H\cup W)=\mathrm{P}(H)+\mathrm{P}(W)-\mathrm{P}(H\cap W)$ or $\mathrm{P}(H'\cap W)=\mathrm{P}(H\cup W)-\mathrm{P}(H)$ M1
$\mathrm{P}(H\cap W)=\dfrac{3}{8}\times \mathrm{P}(W)$ or $\mathrm{P}(H'\cap W)=\mathrm{P}(H')\times \mathrm{P}(W)$ M1
$\dfrac{3}{4}=\dfrac{3}{8}+\mathrm{P}(W)-\dfrac{3}{8}\mathrm{P}(W)$ or $\dfrac{3}{8}=\dfrac{5}{8}\mathrm{P}(W)$ A1
$\mathrm{P}(W)=\dfrac{3}{5}^*$ A1cso*
NB: A method which uses $\frac{3}{5}$ or $\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{3}{8}[=\frac{9}{40}]$ can score maximum M1M1A0A0.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for use of $P(H\cup W)=P(H)+P(W)-P(H\cap W)$ (with at least one value correctly substituted) or use of $P(H'\cap W)=P(H\cup W)-P(H)$ (with at least one value correctly substituted)
- A1 a correct equation in P(W) (allow W or x here)
- A1cso* Correct solution ending with P(W)=$\frac{3}{5}$ with no wrong working seen. Dep. on all previous marks.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The event $N$ is such that
$\mathrm{P}(N)=\dfrac{1}{15} \qquad \mathrm{P}(H\cap N)=\mathrm{P}(N)$
(b) Find $\mathrm{P}(N'|H)$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\mathrm{P}(N'|H)=\dfrac{\frac{3}{8}-\frac{1}{15}}{\frac{3}{8}}$ or $\dfrac{\frac{9}{40}+\frac{1}{12}}{\frac{3}{8}}$ or $1-\dfrac{\frac{1}{15}}{\frac{3}{8}}$ M1
$=\dfrac{37}{45}$ = awrt 0.822 A1
For $\frac{p}{\frac{3}{8}}$ where $0<p<\frac{3}{8}$ use of independence is M0 e.g. $\frac{x\times\frac{3}{8}}{\frac{3}{8}}$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Given that $W$ and $N$ are mutually exclusive,
(c) draw a Venn diagram to represent the events $H$, $W$ and $N$ giving the exact probabilities of each region in the Venn diagram.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) 3 circles labelled. Either N inside H or allow as intersecting circles with $\mathrm{P}(N\cap H')=0$, but do not allow blank space to be considered 0. Condone missing box for this mark. Allow all 3 circles overlapping with all zeros correctly labelled. B1
For $\mathrm{P}(H\cap W)=\frac{3}{8}\times\frac{3}{5}\left[=\frac{9}{40}\right]$ seen or correctly placed in Venn diagram. M1
For their $\frac{3}{5}-"\frac{9}{40}"="\frac{3}{8}"$ (may be implied by the regions in their P(W) adding to 0.6) M1
For their $\frac{3}{8}-"\frac{9}{40}"-\frac{1}{15}="\frac{1}{12}"$ M1
Fully correct diagram with $\frac{1}{4}$ and box and correct probabilities (allow exact decimal equivalents) A1

questions.stem:
A manufacturer fills bottles with oil.
The volume of oil in a bottle, $V\,\text{ml}$, is normally distributed with $V\sim \mathrm{N}(100, 2.5^2)$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\mathrm{P}(V>104.9)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z>\dfrac{104.9-100}{2.5}\right)$ M1
$=1-0.975$ M1
$=0.0250$ (0.025 or awrt 0.0250) A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Standardising with 104.9, 100 and 2.5 (allow $\pm$) implied by 1.96 seen
- M1 For use of $1-p$ with $0.9<p<1$ condone answer of 0.0249 for this mark
- A1 Allow 0.025 or awrt 0.0250 (NB calculator answer is 0.02499….) (answer only scores M1M1A1)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) In a pack of 150 bottles, find the expected number of bottles containing more than $104.9\,\text{ml}$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) Expected number $=150\times"0.025"$ M1
=3.75 awrt 3.75 A1
(iswaft after answer of 3.75 seen. If 3.75 not seen, allow 4 if the method mark is awarded.)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 For $150\times$"their part (a)"

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the value of $v$, to 2 decimal places, such that $\mathrm{P}(V>v \mid V<104.9)=0.2801$
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\left[\mathrm{P}(V>v|V<104.9)=\right]\dfrac{[\mathrm{P}(v<V<104.9)]}{\mathrm{P}(V<104.9)}=0.2801$ M1
$\mathrm{P}(v<V<104.9)=(1-"0.025")-\mathrm{P}(V<v)$ M1
$\mathrm{P}(V<v)=(1-"0.025")-(1-"0.025")\times 0.2801 [=0.7019]$ oe dM1
$\dfrac{v-100}{2.5}=0.53$ M1A1
$v=101.325$ awrt 101.32 or awrt 101.33 A1
ALT: For first two M marks $\frac{\mathrm{P}(V<v)}{\mathrm{P}(V<104.9)}=1-0.2801$ scores M1M1, then follow scheme.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 For writing or using a ratio of probabilities with denominator $P(V<104.9)$ oe and equating to 0.2801 $\frac{p}{P(V<104.9)}=0.2801$ implied by awrt 0.273. Use of independence is M0 e.g. $\frac{x\times P(V<104.9)}{P(V<104.9)}=0.2801$
- M1 For writing or using $P(V>v\cap V<104.9)=P(V<104.9)-P(V<v)[=(1-"0.025")-P(V<v)]$
- dM1 (dep M1) Dependent on previous M1 for rearranging to find $P(V<v)$. Allow equivalent oe $(1-"their(a)")(1-0.2801)$. NB: $[P(V<v)=]$ awrt 0.702 implies M1M1M1 or $[P(V>v)=]$ awrt 0.298 implies M1M1M1
- M1 Standardising with 100, 2.5 and equating to a z-value, $\frac{v-100}{2.5}=z$ $0.4<|z|<0.6$. Watch out for $\frac{v-100}{2.5}=$probability which is M0
- A1 Correct equation with compatible signs
- A1 awrt 101.33 (allow awrt 101.32 from use of calculator)
